subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-13 (kb/Work PB530). 'For floating insertion, at least one insertion symbol shall be specified to the left of the decimal point position' is the ONE composition rule of this clause that Table 10 cannot carry, and the only one of PB530's four rows that was still unenforced on today's tree: the matrix refuses a right-of-point floating string that FOLLOWS a digit (row floating-sign-right and row floating-currency-right each have a blank '9' column), but those rows ADMIT the decimal separator, so a string with nothing but the point to its left passed the walk. Measured before the fix, all four editions: 01 W1 PIC .$$ bound and rendered MOVE 0.5 as [.00]; PIC V$$ as [ $]; PIC .++ as [.00]; PIC B.$$ as [ .00]; PIC V-- as [  ] - an image no rule derives, because 13.18.40.5 rule 6 defines the image only for a string anchored left of the point (a: 'any or all of the LEADING numeric character positions to the left of the decimal point position'; b: all of them, whose result 'is the same as if the floating insertion editing were defined only to the left of the decimal point position'). All seven entries of negative/pb530-picture-floating-left-of-point are now COBOL1934 naming SR29 at 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. The decimal point position has ONE derivation, PictureComposition.DecimalPointPosition ('V' or the decimal separator; else a leading 'P' string's implied point per 13.18.40.4 GR14; else past the last symbol), read by this rule AND by the Table-10 role assignment that splits the eight two-row symbols, so the two cannot disagree about which side a symbol is on. || THE READING: 'at least one insertion symbol' is the FLOATING insertion symbol, not any insertion symbol - a simple-insertion 'B' to the left (PIC B.$$) leaves the floating string with no digit position of its own before the point, which is what rule 6 cannot edit; golden entry PF05 pins that. The rule names FLOATING INSERTION alone and the standard states no analogue for zero suppression, so PIC .ZZ stays legal (golden 85/pb530_picture_floating_anchor_85 A07 renders [.50]) - the complement golden also holds $$.$$ [$1.50], $$.99 [$1.50], $$$$ [ $12], $$V99 [$150], ++.++ [-1.50] and $$$PP [$15], the last because a TRAILING 'P' string puts the assumed point to its RIGHT. || editions: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (FORMAT 1, no edition-varying element). retired-witness: unit:PictureCompositionTests.AFloatingStringRightOfThePoint_IsCOBOLNET1934 (the same witness, re-spelled when the diagnostic code prefix became COBOL#### (kb/Work PB3575); the new spelling is recorded in its place)
